newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam Nike supervisor faces worker abuse trial.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam Nike supervisor faces worker abuse trial.

text.p: A Taiwanese supervisor at a factory in Vietnam which makes Nike Inc shoes will stand trial for allegedly abusing her employees, a Labour Department official in the southern province of Dong Nai said on Monday.

The official, who declined to be named, said police had started prosecution procedures against the woman for allegedly forcing 56 workers to jog twice around the two-km (1.2-mile) factory perimeter for failing to wear regulation workshoes.
According to local newspaper reports, 12 of the women fainted and were taken to hospital.
An official at the factory, which is owned by Taiwan's Pou Chen Corp, said two weeks ago that the supervisor, Hsu Jiu Yun, had been suspended.

The Pou Chen Vietnam Enterprises Limited factory was one of five plants -- three South Korean and two Taiwanese -- producing Nike shoes in Vietnam which were named last week by Vietnam Labour Watch for abuse of their workers.

The labour activist group's Thuyen Nguyen told a news conference in New York that he had found workers at factories contracted by Nike earning less than the minimum wage in the first three months of employment.
Some were limited to one trip to the lavatory and two drinks of water per shift, and verbal abuse, sexual harassment and corporal punishment were common, he said.
A Nike executive said he could not confirm Nguyen's findings but said the company welcomes and works with independent observers to monitor, train and improve working conditions overseas.

"Bring us information we can use, and we'll do our damndest to correct any situations that are wrong," said Dusty Kidd, director of labour practices for the Oregon-based recreational shoe giant. "We're looking for ways to make it better."
